source.title: Information flow control for standard OS abstractions
source.venue: Proceedings of the 21st ACM SIGOPS Symposium on Operating Systems Principles (SOSP '07) / ACM SIGOPS Operating Systems Review

confidence_rationale: SOSP paper with a working system and a directly measured instance of the exact failure MECH-067 posits: in MoinMoin (91,000 LOC, 349 modules) the read-ACL gate is implemented at 41 sites across 22 modules and the write-ACL gate at 19 sites across 12 modules, and at least five ACL-bypass vulnerabilities followed. Replacing that scattered per-site enforcement with a single mediating default-deny label mechanism collapsed the trusted surface to ~1,000 lines. That is MECH-067's CONFIRMING clause instantiated, with counts rather than intuition. Marked down from higher because the domain assumes an ADVERSARY, which REE's leak does not have, and because a demonstration that centralisation helped ONE system is not proof it is required in every system.
failure_signatures: A write permission enforced at N call sites scattered across M modules is omitted at one of them and the omission is invisible until exploited -- measured at 41 read-check sites / 22 modules and 19 write-check sites / 12 modules in a single 91k-LOC application, with at least five resulting ACL-bypass vulnerabilities.

Plug-in or extension code loaded into the same process inherits the host's write authority and can violate the host's own access policy, because the policy is expressed as host-code call sites rather than as a mediated property of the store.

Coarse-granularity mediation leaves a residual hole: once Flume authorises a file open it does not interpose on subsequent reads/writes, so the matrix is only as tight as the granularity at which the chokepoint sits.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Application-level access-control checks scattered across a large codebase are unreliable because any one of them can be omitted; enforcing the policy instead as decentralized information-flow labels at a single user-level reference monitor confines the whole application, so that only bugs in a small isolated trusted module can produce a security violation.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the systems-engineering form of MECH-067. REE's 'per-site local gates' -- MECH-094's hypothesis_tag refusal inside ResidueField.accumulate, the sleep pass's 'named module only' contract, the closure operator's bounded attenuation -- are structurally Moin's 60 ACL call sites: correct individually, unverifiable collectively, and silently incomplete the moment a new write path is added that does not route through one of them. Flume's labels-plus-reference-monitor is structurally the proposed (phase, store, actor) default-deny matrix: authority becomes a property of the store and the actor's label rather than a check the caller remembered to write.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries. (1) Flume defends against an ADVERSARY -- malicious plug-ins, remote exploits -- whereas MECH-067's leak is accidental: a rollout writing to residue because nobody thought about that path. Adversarial settings justify complete mediation at a cost that accidental settings may not. (2) Flume's stores are OS objects with a natural chokepoint (the system call); REE's stores are tensors and Python attributes with no equivalent narrow waist, so the matrix may not be implementable at comparable cost, and the paper's own coarse-granularity file-I/O residue shows what happens when the chokepoint sits at the wrong grain. (3) The paper shows centralised mediation WORKED for one application; it does not test the counterfactual MECH-067's FALSIFYING clause asks about -- whether the local gates, if audited, would have turned out to be sufficient after all.
mapping.source_context: Systems security; user-level reference monitor on Linux; evaluated by porting the MoinMoin wiki (91k LOC Python) with ~1,000 lines of new trusted C++ and ~1,000 lines of Moin modified, at 30-40% throughput cost.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality high: SOSP, working artefact, concrete counts rather than assertion. mapping_fidelity high because the structural analogy is unusually tight -- scattered enforcement sites in a modular codebase is precisely REE's current position. transfer_risk moderate rather than low: the adversary assumption and the absence of a syscall-like chokepoint in ree_core are real disanalogies, and for an architectural claim mapping_fidelity is weighted above source_quality.
